description: Semantic specs for the Shell Command Builder page -- a specialized editor for creating and managing reusable shell commands that serve as building blocks for workflow setup, verification, and completion steps. Users define commands with their text, working directory, platform compatibility, timeout, and organizational metadata. Shell commands can be referenced from any workflow phase, enabling consistent environment preparation, health checks, and cleanup operations across multiple workflows.

groups.name: Shell Command Library Management
groups.description: The left panel shows all saved shell commands in a searchable list using the standard library builder layout pattern. Users can browse their command library, search by name, create new commands, and select existing ones to edit. Each list item displays the command name and key metadata. The split-panel layout places the command list on the left and the editor on the right, consistent with all other builder pages in the runner.

assertions.description: Users see the Shell Commands page title within the standard library builder layout, identifying this as the shell command management interface
Users can create a new shell command that opens a blank editor with default values (any platform, 30 second timeout), ready for command text entry
Users can search through saved shell commands by name to quickly find a specific command for editing or review

groups.name: Command Editor and Configuration
groups.description: The right-panel editor provides all fields for defining a shell command. The command text field is the primary input where users enter the actual shell command or script to execute. Users set a descriptive name, specify a working directory for command execution, select the target platform (any, Windows, Linux, macOS), and configure a timeout in seconds. A category field and tag input support organizational needs. The editor toolbar includes save and delete actions.

assertions.description: Users can enter the shell command text that will be executed, which is the primary and most important field in the command editor
Users can specify the working directory where the command should be executed, ensuring it runs in the correct project or environment context
Users can select the target platform (Any Platform, Windows, Linux, macOS) to ensure commands only run on compatible operating systems
Users can set a timeout in seconds for command execution, preventing hung or long-running commands from blocking workflow progress
Users can save the current command configuration to the library, making it available for use as setup, verification, or completion steps in workflows

groups.name: Organization and Reuse
groups.description: Shell commands support organizational metadata to help users manage large command libraries. Categories group commands by function (e.g., build, test, deploy). Tags provide flexible cross-cutting labels for discovery through the library dashboard. The combination of name, category, and tags ensures commands are easy to find when building workflows, whether through the library dashboard search or the workflow builder's step picker.

assertions.description: Users can assign a category to commands for functional grouping (e.g., build, test, deploy), aiding organization in large command libraries
Users can add tags to commands for flexible labeling and cross-category discovery through the library dashboard
Users can delete commands they no longer need, removing them from the library to keep the command collection clean and relevant
